newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rise on NY strength, Ericsson gains.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rise on NY strength, Ericsson gains.

text.p: A rally in telecommunications group Ericsson, lower interest rates and continued Wall Street strength lifted Swedish share prices higher on Wednesday.
The general index jumped 1.7 percent to 2297.50 with turnover reaching a 1996 record of 7.44 billion crowns. In June, 1994, the all-time high of 10.5 billion was reached.
Ericsson was boosted by afternoon rumours that it and Finnish rival Nokia planned to merge, but dealers did not take the rumours too seriously.
Ericsson leaped 9.5 crowns to 206 crowns, while Nokia was trading at 251.5 markka in after-market-trading, up 3.5.
"There are lots of rumours saying that Ericsson and Nokia will merge, but I do not think that anyone actually believes in them," a broker said.
Mortgage bank Stadshypotek was the day's most traded share after the Finance Inspectorate cleared banking group Handelsbanken's 22.9 billion crown bid on the group.
Stadshypotek rose one crown to 187.5 crowns, while Handelsbanken jumped 8.50 crowns to 198.5 crowns.
Despite Morgan Stanley lowering its recommendation on Astra's shares to "neutral" from "outperform," Astra rose one crown to 322 crowns. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006
